items.title: Clayton Duerr Interview, 1972-04-17
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Well a lot of guys had gone for years, like Joey Bruney's would have been too old even because he was a grown man.

ctx.x: Well you see, like I said, about me leaving here when I was just, if I had stayed around New Orleans when I was 19 and stayed here and worked there for 10 years, you know what I mean? I was out for between 20 and 30, I came back when I was 30 years old, 1936. But I mean that 10 years that I left there, that's why I had met Sharky before I went away and that's why I knew Sharky in New York. I mean there were a lot of other guys, some guys I met right before I left and I didn't see them for a long time, you know…
Well a lot of guys had gone for years, like Joey Bruney's would have been too old even because he was a grown man.

Well I used to, when I moved out here, you see when I first moved out here I was 13 and when I got into music I was about 15 and I started to play. Then when I got to be about 17 I used to go to the Hayd Playhouse and used to do the band over there. Oh yeah? Yeah. Well you could walk over there. Yeah I could walk there, right by the halfway, where the Orkins place is up now. It used to be the Hayd Playhouse. I used to go over there and listen to the band over the back door. Bill Eastwood was playing banjo and…
